summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1b in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Famine/30)

data.turoyo: Mbelan ʕəmran, šoḏíwayna, ʕuzlíwayna ŭ quṣríwayna i+šuqáyoste, mahtíwaynala bayn aš+šarʕe du+rabəʕ, əmblíwaynala li+rawmo, ḥawṭíwaynala, huyowa xud i+čərre du+ḥalwo.
data.translation: We spent our lives, we would card, spin, and also wash the linen, put it into springtime cow patties, bring it to the pond, beat it, it would become like powdered beestings.

rationale: New technical subsense and previously absent Infectum-wa box; explicit linen antecedent and repeated processing sequence.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1b in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Famine/38)

data.turoyo: Ġayṭíwaynala dlo+ḥwoṭo, ġayṭíwaynala bi+rawmo bi+rawmo bi+rawmo tarte+tlaṯ+kore, ŭ bəṯr edi g̊ḥawṭíwaynala hul dhuyowa sibore.
data.translation: We would immerse it without beating, we would immerse it in the pond, in the pond, in the pond two-three times, and then we would beat it until it would become multicoloured.

rationale: Second context for the technical operation; explicitly contrasts preliminary immersion with later beating.

data.turoyo: Ġayṭíwaynala dlo+ḥwoṭo, ġayṭíwaynala bi+rawmo bi+rawmo bi+rawmo tarte+tlaṯ+kore, ŭ bəṯr edi g̊ḥawṭíwaynala hul dhuyowa sibore.
data.translation: We would immerse it without beating, we would immerse it in the pond, in the pond, in the pond two-three times, and then we would beat it until it would become multicoloured.

rationale: First Infinitiv ḥwoṭo, an event noun after without, paired in the same passage with active cloth beating. No Detransitive morphology or patient-subject relation is shown.

One textile-processing account explicitly distinguishes immersion without beating from the subsequent repeated beating stage. The operation recurs at verses 30 and 38; one technical subsense, not multiple senses per form.

summary: All four records were checked. The three textile tokens belong to one technical subsense, represented by two finite contexts and one Infinitiv, from one speaker/account. The ordinary hurling token is already cited at 67/243.

The technical distinction is grounded in the Turoyo procedure, not only in English: explicit cloth, soaking/immersion, dlo+ḥwoṭo, and a later beating stage with a resulting texture/appearance. “Fulling” as a more specific craft classification is not established and is not put in the gloss.

The new Infectum-wa forms have 1pl workers and a feminine -la object referring to the cloth; repeated procedure is explicit. ḥwoṭo names the same active event. An action nominal is not automatically Detransitive.

The existing threat example’s reference to a laundry bat is compatible with the textile use, but these new passages do not name that instrument. No instrument is inserted into their Turoyo or translation.

No claim is made that the craft use is a separate inherited lexeme or that the final colour/texture terms are fully understood. The single numbered subsense remains anchored to the established striking meaning.
Does the named procedure correspond specifically to fulling, to washing by beating, or another textile finishing stage? The proposed gloss states only the securely observed beating during washing.
Confirm the productive nominal status of ḥwoṭo and the editors’ preferred placement. No Detransitive form is established by these clauses.
Clarify the source’s final texture/colour description and its relation to the process, without replacing the edition’s English.
